name: Lightface Celtic Ten-Point 1889
designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimens
foundry: Boston and Central Type Foundries; also shown by American Type Founders
description: The ten-point Light-face Celtic cut, with a wider C and j hook, narrower M and lower small-letter body than the twelve-point cut.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z/a–z, all ten figures, period, comma, semicolon and hyphen. Space is a modern layout advance.
observed: Labelled ten-point alphabets and matching census and job-room impressions support every visible character. Boston and ATF provide named comparison witnesses.
reconstructed: No visible characters invented. Modern spacing and digital metrics, local paper illumination correction and measured rigid rotations. Date suffix identifies an inspected source, not first release.
